result.summary: 这篇论文提出了“精度感知”的缩放定律，用于预测低精度训练和训练后量化对语言模型损失的影响 [abstract]。作者提出低精度训练会降低模型的有效参数量，并据此预测低精度训练和训练后量化带来的额外损失 [abstract]。研究发现，训练后量化带来的退化会随着模型训练数据量的增加而增大，最终使额外的预训练数据变得有害 [abstract]。作者在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，并在最多 1.7B 参数、最多 26B token 的模型上验证了预测 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：精度、参数量和数据之间存在怎样的权衡，以及这些权衡在预训练和推理中有何不同 [S1.p1]。研究动机在于，精度是影响模型成本和性能的第三个重要因素，而当前的缩放定律并未考虑这一点 [S1.p1][abstract]。

evidence.quote: However, the precision in which models are trained and served is an important third factor that contributes to both cost and performance.
Specifically, we ask: What are the tradeoffs between precision, parameters, and data? How do they compare for pretraining and inference?
Low precision training and inference affect both the quality and cost of language models, but current scaling laws do not account for this.

method.text: 论文提出“精度感知”的缩放定律，其核心思想是：比特精度和参数量可以互换地贡献于模型的“有效参数量” N_eff，而量化实现细节仅通过影响该量来与损失缩放交互 [S1.p2]。作者将训练后量化和预训练量化的缩放定律统一为单一函数形式，以预测不同精度下训练和推理带来的退化 [abstract]。

evidence.quote: This functional form that posits bit precision and parameter count interchangeably contribute to a model’s “effective parameter count,” $N_{\text{eff}}$, and implementation details like which parts of a model are quantized to what precision, interact with loss scaling only through their effect on this quantity.
We unify the scaling laws for post and pretraining quantization to arrive at a single functional form that predicts degradation from training and inference in varied precisions.

experiments.text: 作者在 Dolma V1.7 数据集上训练和评估了一系列 OLMo 风格的模型，使用标准 Transformer++ 实现 [S2.SS3.p1]。实验扫描了非嵌入参数量 N 在 3 千万到 2.2 亿之间、数据量 D 在 15 亿到 260 亿 token 之间的预训练运行，并在每个 (N,D) 组合上启动超过 20 次运行，扫描 8 种精度值 [S2.SS3.p1]。训练精度 P_w、P_a、P_kv 分别在 [3,12] 范围内单独扫描，并预训练了任意组合的模型以验证缩放定律 [S4.p1]。

evidence.quote: We train and evaluate a suite of OLMo-style models on the Dolma V1.7 dataset, using a standard Transformer++ implementation
Our experiments consist of a sweep of language model pretraining runs over $N\in[30,60,110,220]$ million parameters (non-embedding) and $D\in[1.5,3,6,13,26]$ billion tokens.
we sweep 8 values of precision for each of the (weights, activations, attention).
We sweep the training precisions of the weights, activations, and KV cache $P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}}\in[3,12]$ individually, as well as training BF16 baselines.
We also pretrain models with arbitrary combinations of $P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}}$ to validate our scaling laws.

findings.text: 训练后量化带来的损失退化随数据量增加而增大，因此对于固定模型，在某个点之后继续用更多数据训练，如果模型之后会被量化，可能反而有害 [S1.p3][S3.p1]。在量化训练中，权重的比特精度可以与参数量进行权衡，即较小 N 但较大 P_w 的模型可以达到与较大 N 但较小 P_w 的模型相同的损失，且增加权重比特精度的收益在低精度时较大，但在约 6-7 比特后饱和 [S4.SS1.p1]。预训练缩放定律表明，计算最优的预训练精度通常与计算预算无关，但如果模型大小受限，这种独立性不再成立，此时计算最优精度随计算量缓慢增长 [S1.p3]。

evidence.quote: We find that the degradation increases with data, so that for a fixed model, training on additional data after a certain point can be actively harmful if the model will be quantized after training.
We quantify the resulting loss degradation $\delta_{\text{PTQ}}$, finding that post-train quantization scales poorly in data.

We observe that the bit precision of the weights can be traded off for the number of parameters, i.e., a model with smaller $N$ but larger $P_{\text{w}}$ can achieve the same loss as a model with larger $N$ but smaller $P_{\text{w}}$.
Additionally, we find that the gains from increasing the bit precision of the weights are large at lower precisions but saturate at higher precisions (typically around 6-7 bits per weight).
Our scaling laws for pretraining suggest that the compute-optimal pretraining precision is in general independent of compute budget.
Surprisingly, however, this independence ceases to be true if model size is constrained, in which case the compute-optimal precision grows slowly in compute.

limitations.text: 作者承认以下局限：全程使用固定架构来考察精度、参数和 token 的影响，而低精度训练常涉及架构调整，可能缩小与全精度模型的差距 [S6.p2]。虽然计算成本随精度线性缩放，但由于系统开销，减半精度带来的收益通常不到 2 倍 [S6.p2]。研究仅考虑损失缩放，未进行下游模型评估 [S6.p2]。作者强调所发现的趋势旨在提供启示而非规定性结论，并希望未来工作能在更大模型规模上更全面地检验这些效应 [S6.p2]。

evidence.quote: First, we use a fixed architecture throughout to examine the effects of precision, parameters, and tokens in a controlled manner.
In contrast, low precision training often involves architectural tweaks that can close much of the gap from a vanilla full precision model.
Second, while compute costs do scale linearly with precision, the gains from halving precision are usually less than 2x due to systems overhead.
Third, we only consider loss scaling without downstream model evaluations.
We emphasize that the trends we find aim to be suggestive rather than prescriptive, and hope future work can more comprehensively examine these effects at larger model scale.
